sessions.name: A
sessions.reply:
The command that works, run from the project root (`<run>\work\L1\c\w`):

```
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Both tests pass: `test_transfer_preserves_total` and `test_rejects_non_positive_amount`.

Without `PYTHONPATH=src`, the run fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'ledgerlite'`. The package sits in a `src/` layout and isn't installed, so Python can't find it. There's no `pyproject.toml` or `setup.py` to install it from, so I didn't change any files.

That command uses Git Bash syntax. In PowerShell it would be `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"; python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.

sessions.name: B
sessions.reply:
I added `Ledger.close(name)` in `src/ledgerlite/__init__.py`. It raises `ValueError` if the account's balance isn't zero. Otherwise it removes the account. An unknown name raises `KeyError`, the same as `balance()` does.

I also added `test_close_requires_zero_balance` in `tests/test_ledger.py`. It checks that closing a non-zero account raises and leaves the account in place. It then checks that the account closes once its balance is back to zero.

The full suite passes: 3 tests, all OK. I ran it with `PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`. Without `PYTHONPATH=src` the import of `ledgerlite` fails, as the project notes said it would.
